title: autotrade — when trades have accumulated: review the ladder, then revise one rule
_why: Revision, not discovery. Step 0 walks the ladder from the ledger with no model involved, so a
strategy that stopped working is demoted before anything else happens. Step 1 picks the one
rule to work on — worst first, then least recently revised — and hands over its current
parameters, its live record and what has already been refused for it.
One per run because a loop cannot carry six chained steps per item: inside a FOREACH the
steps chain through $prev only, so a per-strategy body could not reach back to its own runs.
Rotating one at a time is honest about that rather than pretending the loop would work.
Step 2 is the model's only move, and it is bounded to the neighbourhood of a rule that already
runs. If the revision clears the bar the same strategy is updated and its ladder restarts —
the record that earned the old stage was earned by a different rule.
Hourly, because the trigger is not the clock. Crypto never closes, so 'after the close' is
not a moment; what carries new information is a completed entry-to-exit cycle. next_revision
offers nothing until `minClosedTrips` of them have finished since the rule was last written,
so most runs stop at step 2's CONDITION and cost nothing. On a market that does close, the
same declaration still works — the trades simply only accumulate during session hours.

pipeline.instruction:
You are given one trading rule that is currently running, its live record, what its backtest promised, and the history of what has already been refused for it. Answer with a JSON object only — no prose — describing where to search for a better version of THIS rule.

Shape:
{"families":[...],"fast":[...],"slow":[...],"low":[...],"high":[...],"stopLossPct":[...],"takeProfitPct":[...],"holdout":0.3}

families is any of: ma-cross, ema-cross, rsi, bollinger, macd. Stay in the neighbourhood of the current parameters — this is a revision, not a fresh search, so keep the same family unless the record shows it stopped working entirely, and vary the periods around what is running now. null is allowed in stopLossPct and takeProfitPct to mean no stop.

Read the refusals. A combination refused for too few trades will be refused again at the same parameters: slower parameters trade less, faster ones trade more. Keep the space under about 120 combinations — a wider search finds a better-looking result without finding a better rule.

nothingToRevise: With no adopted strategy the CONDITION ends the run at step 2 — cleanly, as an early exit.
That is the state on day one: run discover.example.json once to create the first rule.
whatIsMeasured: The candle loop runs over the symbols this rule actually traded since its stage began, which
the ledger knows and a declared universe does not. A screened rule trades whatever came up
that day; scoring it on a list written months ago would score it on names it never touched.
Capped at eight, busiest first, so a day with forty names still finishes.
A rule that traded nothing yields an empty list and the run ends there — there is nothing to
re-measure until it has a record.
